tool_input.description: Quick scratch check of edge-case behaviors

result:
Only my `NumberUtilsAgentTest` exists (69 tests run total, matching), and it compiled and ran cleanly against the rest of the suite with no conflicts.

The test class `NumberUtilsAgentTest` is complete, with 69 tests covering constants, all `compare` overloads, `createBigDecimal`/`createBigInteger`/`createDouble`/`createFloat`/`createInteger`/`createLong`, extensive `createNumber` boundary cases (hex/octal/overflow/type suffixes/malformed input), `isCreatable`/`isNumber`/`isDigits`/`isParsable`, all `max`/`min` array and 3-arg overloads with null/empty/NaN handling, the `to*` conversion methods with defaults, and `toScaledBigDecimal` overloads.

Two tests fail, and both point to a real bug in `NumberUtils.createNumber`/`createBigInteger`:

- **`testIsCreatableInvalidNumbers`** and **`testCreateNumberDoubleSignThrows`**: `NumberUtils.createNumber("--1")` returns `BigInteger` `1` instead of throwing `NumberFormatException`, and `NumberUtils.isCreatable("--1")` returns `true`. The string `"--1"` is not valid Java number syntax, but `createBigInteger` strips one leading sign, then passes the remainder (`"-1"`) straight to `new BigInteger(..., radix)`, which parses the second `-` as a valid negative sign; the method's own `negate` flag then flips that already-negative value positive, so the invalid double-signed input silently round-trips to `1`.
